Tagline: Pantone's 2026 Colour of the Year, on your nails
What it is: Pantone named Cloud Dancer its 2026 Colour of the Year and the nail world translated it into a translucent, creamy white that reads as a milkshake glow rather than flat white-out. Artists keep it airy - two sheer coats over the natural nail, free edge still visible - and let gloss do the luxury part.
Palette / finish: Sheer creamy off-white (#F4F1EC to #E8E2D9), satin to high gloss
Best shape: Short almond, squoval or short round
Ask your nail tech: Sheer milky white, two thin coats, no visible brushstrokes, high-gloss top coat.
Sources: Good Housekeeping; ELLE UK; Harper's Bazaar UK; Marie Claire

Tagline: "Your nails but better" - the polished bare nail
What it is: Vogue lists ultra-sheer washes among its seven biggest trends: a single veil of warm pink, peach or tea-rose tint that evens out the nail bed without hiding it. Sundays Studio describes the effect as "sunshine on water" - warm, natural and flattering across skin tones, which is why it books year-round.
Palette / finish: Tea rose, peach and warm pink veils (#F6E4DE to #E6C3B8), gloss
Best shape: Any; best on short squoval or round
Ask your nail tech: One coat of sheer warm pink, cuticle-clean, glass top coat - nothing opaque.
Sources: Vogue; Harper's Bazaar UK; Marie Claire (spring)

Tagline: The Korean jelly nail becomes the default neutral
What it is: Syrup-gel colour with a wet, see-through depth that makes nails read as "juicy". Good Housekeeping's experts call it "the best version of a naked nail, but smooth and ultra shiny"; on deeper skin tones it behaves as a glossed tint rather than a colour. ELLE files the same finish under "glassy glow".
Palette / finish: Syrupy rose, peach, cherry-cola, clear overlay (#F5D9CF to #D8A899)
Best shape: Short oval, squoval, medium almond
Peak season: Spring/summer; returns as syrup browns in autumn
Ask your nail tech: Jelly/syrup gel in a translucent rose, three thin coats, high-build gloss top.
Sources: Good Housekeeping; ELLE UK; Marie Claire

Tagline: Chrome loses the mirror, gains the glow
What it is: Harper's Bazaar's Juanita Huber-Millet describes 2026 chrome as "whisper-thin metallic washes over nudes, or pearlescent sheens layered over warm browns... less mirror shine, more soft luminosity". It is the glazed-doughnut finish matured into something quieter and more expensive-looking.
Palette / finish: Pearl, champagne and soft silver washes (#DCD9D2 to #EFE9DF)
Best shape: Almond, oval or squoval; short works too
Peak season: All year; peaks in party season
Ask your nail tech: Pearl chrome powder over a warm nude - keep it a soft sheen, not mirror.
Sources: Harper's Bazaar UK; ELLE UK; Allure (fall colour)

Tagline: Cat-eye velvet with a chrome overlay
What it is: Two 2026 favourites collided. Vogue predicts velvet nails finished with a cat-eye magnetic pull and a chrome overlay, giving a soft brush-stroke shimmer that shifts as the hand moves - all the texture of glitter with none of the grit. ILNP's Ritual and Kiss's Fine n Cool press-ons are the high-street route in.
Palette / finish: Dusty mauve, gunmetal and soft navy (#6E6A78 to #B9B2C4)
Best shape: Medium almond or oval - velvet reads best on longer beds
Ask your nail tech: Velvet cat-eye gel with a chrome topper, magnetic pull front to back.
Sources: Vogue; Good Housekeeping; ELLE UK

Tagline: Pigment pulled into halos, bands and domes
What it is: Magnetic pigment is pulled with a magnet into a band, a halo or a 3D dome. Artist Emi Kudo layers Apres Astral Gels over a dark base (Midnight Shadow) for a shimmer that looks lit from inside; Good Housekeeping notes the effect is now routinely combined with charms or a chrome overlay.
Palette / finish: Ink, plum, bronze or emerald bases with magnetic shimmer
Best shape: Almond, coffin, oval
Ask your nail tech: Cat-eye gel over a dark base, magnetic halo effect, no craft glitter.
Sources: Good Housekeeping; Vogue; ELLE UK

Tagline: Liquid metal, worn as jewellery
What it is: Full-coverage liquid metal - silver, gold, bronze - was the loudest finish of the fall 2026 shows and feeds the celestial trend. Allure's fall colour report names molten silver the season's "treat yourself" shade: it reads as jewellery on short nails and as armour on long almond or coffin tips.
Palette / finish: Molten silver, antique gold, bronze (#C8C9CC, #D4B878, #A9744F)
Best shape: Short squoval, or long almond/coffin
Ask your nail tech: Full-coverage chrome or metallic silver, no glitter particles, mirror top coat.
Sources: Allure (fall colour); Good Housekeeping; ELLE UK

Tagline: The glass nail, sculpted instead of just shiny
What it is: Allure's "blown glass" and Good Housekeeping's "ribbed glass" push the glass nail into three dimensions: sculpted bubbles, fine ribs and holographic layers sealed under a clear dome. The spring 2026 runways did the same thing at Head of State, where nails looked literally glass-blown.
Palette / finish: Clear, icy blue and pearl with holographic shifts
Best shape: Short-to-medium almond; sculpture needs length
Ask your nail tech: Clear builder gel sculpted into ribs or bubbles, holographic flake, high dome.
Sources: Allure; Good Housekeeping; Harper's Bazaar (runway)

Tagline: Caramel, chai and butter beige
What it is: Harper's Bazaar calls them "comfort colours": caramel, chai latte, buttery beige and warm mocha. Worn sheer-to-medium, these are what clients ask for when they want something cosier than a nude but safer than a colour - the palette equivalent of a cashmere throw.
Palette / finish: Caramel, chai, butter beige, mocha (#C8A279 to #E0C9AE)
Best shape: Any; almond and short squoval lead
Ask your nail tech: Warm caramel nude, sheer-to-medium coverage, gloss.
Sources: Harper's Bazaar UK; Marie Claire

Tagline: Mocha cools down and goes deeper
What it is: The mocha of 2024-25 has cooled and deepened. Good Housekeeping flags cool-toned browns; Allure's fall 2026 report leads with "cozy browns" such as JinSoon Earth Clay (sent down Proenza Schouler) and Essie Never Skip a Beat, plus red-browns like Orly Canyon Clay. Marie Claire's autumn story is the same coffee mood.
Palette / finish: Cocoa, espresso, taupe-brown (#6B4B3A to #4A322A)
Best shape: Medium almond or square
Ask your nail tech: Cool espresso brown, opaque, satin or gloss.
Sources: Good Housekeeping; Allure (fall colour); Marie Claire

Tagline: Brick, bordeaux and cherry instead of bright tomato
What it is: Red, but grown up. Harper's Bazaar calls it "matured reds" - brick, wine and Bordeaux - while Allure's fall cherry is deeper still: Hermes Rouge H, Dazzle Dry Fast-Track Cherry and Nailboo's cola-toned Cola Kiss. Opaque, high-shine and unadorned; the colour is the whole design.
Palette / finish: Brick, bordeaux, merlot, cherry (#7E1F26 to #5C1218)
Best shape: Short almond or squoval; classic on oval
Ask your nail tech: Deep bordeaux red, opaque, high-gloss - no shimmer.
Sources: Harper's Bazaar UK; Allure (fall colour); Marie Claire

Tagline: Jewel-box sapphire meets bright cobalt
What it is: Blue split into two moods: the sapphire of Allure's fall 2026 report (shades such as Sapphire Season and Playing With Sapphire) and the electric and aquamarine blues of spring. Good Housekeeping lists electric blue among the year's most-requested colours; ELLE's "cool blue" layers it under a silver chrome topper.
Palette / finish: Sapphire, electric cobalt, icy aquamarine (#1F3A6E, #2F6FB5, #7FC7D9)
Best shape: Short square or squoval for brights; almond for sapphire
Ask your nail tech: Opaque sapphire (or electric cobalt), gloss; chrome topper optional.
Sources: Good Housekeeping; ELLE UK; Allure (fall colour); Marie Claire (spring)

Tagline: Olive, moss and chartreuse
What it is: Olive, moss and chartreuse moved from the runway to the fingers. Allure's fall 2026 greens - Lights Lacquer Extra Dirty, Gel Jukebox Olive, The Stranger - are muddy and wearable; Marie Claire puts chartreuse at the loud end of the same family. Matte top coat makes them read modern rather than retro.
Palette / finish: Olive, moss, chartreuse (#6B6B3A, #4E5B31, #A8B36A)
Best shape: Short squoval; chartreuse on almond
Ask your nail tech: Muddy olive green, opaque, matte or satin top coat.
Sources: Allure (fall colour); Marie Claire

Tagline: Black that reveals its colour in daylight
What it is: The compromise between black and colour: near-black plum, midnight navy and oxblood that read black indoors and show their hue in sunlight. Allure's fall list bundles Essie Wicked, OPI Lincoln Park After Dark and Manucurist Hollyhock; the winter pedicure story pushes the same idea into multichrome.
Palette / finish: Near-black plum, midnight navy, oxblood (#1A1418 to #2B1E26)
Best shape: Short oval, almond, square
Ask your nail tech: Near-black plum, two coats, gloss - dark but not flat black.
Sources: Allure (fall colour); Marie Claire

Tagline: Lilac, butter yellow and peach blossom
What it is: The "Goldilocks" shades Allure describes as neither summery-bright nor wintry-dark. Lilac was fall 2026's surprise, butter yellow keeps rolling through 2026 and Marie Claire's spring list adds peach blossom and powder pink - all best in a cloudy, milky finish rather than a flat creme.
Palette / finish: Lilac, butter yellow, peach blossom, powder pink (#C9B8D8, #F3E3A8, #F6D3C4)
Best shape: Short almond or squoval
Ask your nail tech: Cloudy lilac (or butter yellow) - sheer and milky, never neon.
Sources: Allure (fall colour); Marie Claire (spring)

Tagline: 2026's successor to the polka dot
What it is: Allure's number-one art trend: pinstripes, barcode stripes, awning stripes and the "athletic sock" tip Miss Pop painted at Alice + Olivia spring/summer 2026 - two thin horizontal lines across a bare or white tip. Good Housekeeping's retro striped French stacks colour bands instead of one solid tip.
Palette / finish: Contrast pairs: red/white, black/cream, navy/pink
Best shape: Square or squoval - stripes need a straight tip
Ask your nail tech: Two thin horizontal stripes across the tip, crisp edges, gloss.
Sources: Allure; Good Housekeeping; Harper's Bazaar (runway)

Tagline: The dot shrinks to 1-2 mm
What it is: After 2025's full-size dots, 2026 does them micro: one or two millimetre spots in a scattered or grid layout, or a single dot per nail. ELLE names micro polka dots among its eight biggest trends, and Good Housekeeping points out a toothpick is enough to DIY the whole set.
Palette / finish: Monochrome, tonal nudes, or one accent colour on Cloud Dancer white
Best shape: Short round or squoval
Ask your nail tech: Micro dots, 1-2 mm, evenly spaced, on a sheer milky base.
Sources: Good Housekeeping; ELLE UK; Marie Claire (spring)

Tagline: The French tip, set with stones
What it is: The French tip got jewellery: crystal-studded tips, silver studs and rhinestone rows over a crisp neutral base. "It's like jewelry for your nails," artist Sofi Mazur tells Allure; Valeriia Telemaniuk recommends a proper crystal adhesive rather than sticking gems onto wet gel, which "will pop off in two days".
Palette / finish: Nude base plus clear crystal, silver or multicolour rhinestones
Best shape: Almond or square; short French also works
Ask your nail tech: Slim French tip covered in small crystals, set with crystal adhesive, no bulky gel.
Sources: Allure; Harper's Bazaar UK

Tagline: Diffused tips, tonal instead of white-on-pink
What it is: The French softened: ultra-slim tips, diffused edges and tonal pairs - milky base with an off-white tip, or chocolate over caramel. Who What Wear's "cloudy French" and Good Housekeeping's "milky French" describe the same airbrushed edge, and it is the most wearable nail-art trend of the year.
Palette / finish: Milky base + off-white tip; caramel + chocolate; sheer pink + white
Best shape: Short almond, oval or squoval
Ask your nail tech: Soft diffused French, very thin tip, off-white on milky, no harsh line.
Sources: Harper's Bazaar UK; Good Housekeeping; Who What Wear; Allure

Tagline: Ralph Lauren energy, painted on
What it is: Vogue's prep-school plaid and Good Housekeeping's argyle ride the argyle-knit revival: jelly plaid, diamonds with fine criss-cross lines, or dark-academia colourways built from a jewel base. Kylie Jenner's jelly plaid by Zola Ganzorigt is the reference image clients bring to the salon.
Palette / finish: Jewel tones, burgundy, forest, cream with fine white lines
Best shape: Square, squoval or short almond
Ask your nail tech: Plaid or argyle: jelly base, thin white criss-cross lines, one accent diamond.
Sources: Vogue; Good Housekeeping

Tagline: Runway fabric becomes a nail technique
What it is: Chanel under Matthieu Blazy is the reference: tweed, woven texture, lace and silk translated onto the nail. Vogue lists both Chanel tweed and lace-and-silk among its seven trends; Who What Wear's lace art wears the same idea as an accent nail or under a French tip, with Cloud Dancer as the base.
Palette / finish: Boucle cream, tweed multi-tones, black lace over Cloud Dancer
Best shape: Short almond or oval - texture needs a small canvas
Ask your nail tech: Hand-painted lace (or tweed) on one accent nail, matte top coat to fake fabric.
Sources: Vogue; Who What Wear

Tagline: Moon dust, crystals and a ring of colour
What it is: Two star-themed looks dominate. "Extra celestial" - silver metallic, crystals, 3D charms and hardware that reads outer space - was flagged by Pinterest for 2026; halo nails draw a ring of polish around the nail edge instead of a tip (Dua Lipa wore them). Both work as one accent nail or a full set.
Palette / finish: Moon-dust silver and pearl; halos in contrast brights
Best shape: Almond and oval for halo; any for celestial
Ask your nail tech: Silver chrome with a few crystals at the cuticle, or a 2 mm halo outline.
Sources: Who What Wear; ELLE UK; Marie Claire

Tagline: Rings, studs and bangles, worn on the nail
What it is: Actual jewellery: tiny rings, bars and studs pierced through the free edge or set into gel, plus Good Housekeeping's "bangles nails" - stacked gold, silver or rose-gold bands with gemstones. Allure pairs black polish with "a piercing (or five)". The look is punk rather than precious.
Palette / finish: Black, cherry or nude base plus gold/silver hardware
Best shape: Square or almond with enough free edge to pierce
Ask your nail tech: One gold ring through the tip plus a stud at the base; drill and seal properly.
Sources: Allure; Good Housekeeping

Tagline: 3D, but quiet - pearls and soft gel swirls
What it is: Three dimensions, restrained: micro pearls, delicate studs, soft gel swirls and negative space instead of 2025's charm-heavy maximalism. Harper's Bazaar calls it "sculpted minimalism"; Good Housekeeping notes 3D gel swirls coated in chrome powder for a harder, more graphic finish.
Palette / finish: Tonal nudes with pearl, chrome or gold accents
Best shape: Short almond or squoval; keep sculpture to 1-2 nails
Ask your nail tech: One sculpted pearl or chrome swirl per hand over a sheer nude, negative space.
Sources: Harper's Bazaar UK; Vogue; Good Housekeeping; Who What Wear

Tagline: Leopard, deer print and horse motifs
What it is: Leopard, deer print and horse motifs - Good Housekeeping labels the trend "bambicore" - replace last year's tortoiseshell. Vogue's Chanel reference pushes a refined leopard in muted browns, and Marie Claire's October 2026 report confirms animal print as the season's art story. Keep it tonal so it reads expensive rather than fancy-dress.
Palette / finish: Camel, cocoa, cream and black spots
Best shape: Almond, oval or short square
Ask your nail tech: Tonal leopard on two or three nails, brown on cream, tiny spots, matte top.
Sources: Good Housekeeping; Vogue; Marie Claire

Tagline: Mismatched hands, on purpose
What it is: The counter-trend: mismatched hands, clashing colours, matte against shiny 3D, Y2K references. Allure's "mixed maximalist" and ELLE's "glitchy glam" describe the same instinct - deliberate asymmetry after years of clean-girl minimalism - and it is the easiest trend to DIY because there are no rules.
Palette / finish: Anything: one matte, one gloss and one metallic per set
Best shape: Mixed shapes across hands (short plus medium)
Ask your nail tech: Mismatched set: one hand matte brights, one hand gloss nudes, same accent charm.
Sources: Allure; ELLE UK; Who What Wear

Tagline: Shape is the hero, colour is the support
What it is: The salon default for 2026. Harper's Bazaar's experts say shape is now "the hero, with colour and art as supporting details"; Vogue lists sculpted almond among its seven trends, and Pure Nails' 2026 shape report still puts almond as the single most-requested shape because it lengthens the hand without stiletto maintenance.
Palette / finish: Works with every finish; chrome and velvet look best
Best shape: Sculpted almond / elongated oval, medium length
Ask your nail tech: Medium almond, apex at the stress point, tapered but not pointed.
Sources: Harper's Bazaar UK; Vogue; Good Housekeeping; Pure Nails

Tagline: The square comeback, with rounded corners
What it is: The surprise of the spring 2026 runways: square tips returned, but soft - gently rounded corners rather than the sharp 2000s block. Harper's Bazaar's runway report leads with square as spring's biggest shape story and notes extra-long coffin as its exaggerated cousin; Good Housekeeping lists square among the year's key shapes.
Palette / finish: Best with brights, stripes and French tips
Best shape: Soft square, short to medium
Ask your nail tech: Soft square - straight sides, corners filed round, medium length.
Sources: Harper's Bazaar (runway); Good Housekeeping; Pure Nails

Tagline: The practical winner of 2026
What it is: Squoval is strong like a square, soft like an oval and the least likely to snag. ELLE calls it the "Squoval Revival"; Harper's Bazaar's "short and sweet" pairs it with sheer, milky colour; Pure Nails rates it the easiest shape to maintain and among the strongest - which is why it is the default for anyone with an active life.
Palette / finish: Sheers, milky whites, soft chromes
Best shape: Squoval / short oval
Ask your nail tech: Short squoval, rounded corners, sheer milky colour, glass top coat.
Sources: ELLE UK; Harper's Bazaar UK; Pure Nails; Good Housekeeping

Tagline: The statement shape at the far end
What it is: Extra-long coffin appeared at Knwls, and Naomi Yasuda built a curved, feline "cat-claw" shape for L'Enchanteur - a dramatic C-curve that follows the finger. Both are extension territory, and the shapes that carry chrome, molten metallics and 3D sculpture best.
Palette / finish: Chrome, molten metallic, 3D embellishment
Best shape: Coffin or cat-claw (curved)
Ask your nail tech: Long coffin with a deep C-curve, or a cat-claw taper; expect extensions.
Sources: Harper's Bazaar (runway); Pure Nails
